message.abstract: The rapid expansion of generative AI in higher education underscores the need to understand how students’ ethical awareness and language competencies shape the quality of AI-assisted academic decisions. This study investigates how ethical awareness and English language fluency influence students’ perceived usefulness of artificial intelligence (AI) and its subsequent impact on decision quality in higher education contexts. Drawing on a survey of 409 undergraduate students from private universities in Indonesia, the study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test a revised conceptual model with improved measurement validity. The results demonstrate that ethical awareness significantly enhances perceived usefulness of AI (β = 0.594, p < 0.001) and directly improves decision quality (β = 0.291, p < 0.001). English language fluency also independently predicts decision quality (β = 0.230, p < 0.001), while perceived AI usefulness exerts a strong positive effect on decision quality (β = 0.406, p < 0.001). Ethical awareness also directly contributes to decision quality, indicating its dual role in shaping both evaluative perceptions and decision outcomes. However, English language fluency does not significantly moderate the relationship between perceived usefulness and decision quality, suggesting that its influence operates primarily as an independent cognitive resource rather than an interactional factor. The revised model achieves satisfactory convergent validity and improved model fit, strengthening the robustness of the findings. These results contribute to the literature by clarifying the cognitive and ethical mechanisms through which students engage with AI-assisted decision-making. Practical implications highlight the importance of integrating ethical literacy and language competence into AI education to enhance decision effectiveness.
title: Ethical Awareness, Translanguaging-based EFL Proficiency, and AI Usefulness Predict Decision Quality among University Students
